questions.question: Which Indian woman was the pioneer in winning a silver medal at the Olympic Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P.V. Sindhu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **P.V. Sindhu** became the first Indian woman to win a silver medal at the Olympic Games during the **2016 Rio Olympics**.
 
• She secured the silver medal in the sport of **badminton**, competing in the women's singles category.
 
• Sindhu faced Spain's **Carolina Marin** in the final match, which was a highly competitive and closely fought game.
 
• Her achievement marked a historic moment for Indian sports, making her a national icon and inspiring many young athletes.
 
• P.V. Sindhu is also the second Indian athlete to win an Olympic medal in badminton, following **Saina Nehwal's bronze medal** in the 2012 London Olympics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Olympic Medal in Badminton:** Badminton became an Olympic sport in 1992, and India has since gained significant recognition in the sport, producing world-class players like P.V. Sindhu and Saina Nehwal.
 
• **Women's Singles Badminton:** This event requires exceptional agility, speed, and precision. P.V. Sindhu is known for her powerful smashes and tactical gameplay.
 
• **Achievements of P.V. Sindhu:** Besides her Olympic silver, Sindhu has won multiple medals at the World Badminton Championships, including a gold in 2019.
 
• **Recognition:** P.V. Sindhu has been honored with prestigious awards like the Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri, and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna for her contributions to Indian sports.
 
• **Training and Mentor:** Sindhu trained under the guidance of renowned coach **Pullela Gopichand**, a former All England Open champion, at his academy in Hyderabad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Miscellaneous Tree Crops & Groves:** This category represents privately owned land under orchards and fruit trees, making it match with description 2.
 
• **Culturable Wasteland:** Refers to land left uncultivated for more than five years, aligning with description 3.
 
• **Current Fallow:** Describes land left fallow for one or less than one year, which corresponds to description 4.
 
• **Fallow other than Current Fallow:** Indicates land left fallow for more than one year but less than five years, matching description 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Land-Use Categories:** A classification system used in geography and agriculture to define how different land types are utilized for various purposes like cultivation, forestry, and habitation.
 
• **Fallow Land:** Land that is temporarily not cultivated to allow soil recovery and maintain fertility.

• **Miscellaneous Tree Crops & Groves:** Represents land utilized for growing fruit-bearing trees, orchards, or other grove plantations, generally for commercial purposes.
 
• **Current vs. Non-Current Fallow:** Current fallow refers to land left unused for a short period (less than a year), while non-current fallow pertains to land left idle for longer durations (1-5 years or more).

questions.question:
Which of the following factors contributes to the low child sex ratio in some economically developed Northern states of India?

1) Increased accessibility to prenatal sex-determination methods

2) High levels of female literacy and empowerment

3) Societal preference for male children in inheritance and family support

4) Strengthened enforcement of gender-equal policies
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Increased accessibility to prenatal sex-determination methods** has contributed to the declining child sex ratio in some states due to misuse for sex-selective abortions.
 
• A **societal preference for male children** persists in Northern states, driven by cultural norms favoring sons for inheritance, lineage, and old-age support.
 
• Despite economic development, deeply rooted **patriarchal attitudes** often result in discriminatory practices against female children.
 
• The misuse of medical technologies such as **ultrasound imaging** for prenatal sex determination has led to skewed sex ratios in economically developed regions.
 
• Legal frameworks like the **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act** exist but face challenges in enforcement, allowing misuse to persist.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):** CSR refers to the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the 0-6 age group. It is a key indicator of gender equality and societal attitudes toward female children.
 
• **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act:** Enacted in 1994, this law aims to prevent the misuse of prenatal diagnostic techniques for sex-selective abortions.
 
• **Gender Preferences:** Cultural factors in India often place higher value on male children due to their role in family lineage, economic support, and rituals such as funeral rites.
 
• **Skewed Sex Ratio Consequences:** A declining child sex ratio can lead to long-term societal issues, including gender-based violence, trafficking, and imbalanced marriage markets.
 
• **Government Initiatives:** Campaigns such as **"Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao"** aim to address gender-based discrimination and promote the survival, protection, and education of girls.

questions.question: Sattriya, one of the classical dances of India, was introduced by which saint?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sankardev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India.
 
• It was introduced by the Vaishnavite saint **Sankardev** in the 15th-16th centuries in Assam.
 
• The dance form was originally a medium to narrate and propagate **Vaishnavism** and teachings of Lord Krishna.
 
• Sattriya derives its name from “Satras,” the monasteries established by Sankardev to promote Vaishnavism.
 
• In 2000, the Sattriya dance was recognized as a **classical dance form** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India’s National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sankardev:**

 
 
• A 15th-century saint-scholar, poet, and cultural icon from Assam.
 
• He was the pioneer of the Neo-Vaishnavite movement in the region.
 
• His contributions include writings like the "Kirtan Ghoxa" and translations of scriptures into Assamese.
 
 
 
• **Sattras:**
 
 
• Monastic institutions established by Sankardev to promote Vaishnavism.
 
• They serve as cultural and religious centers, preserving traditional art forms like Sattriya dance and music.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnavism:**
 
 
• A sect of Hinduism focused on the devotion to Lord Vishnu and his avatars, particularly Krishna and Rama.
 
• Sankardev emphasized the path of Bhakti (devotion) as a means to attain spiritual salvation.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya Dance Elements:**
 
 
• It incorporates both **Nritta** (pure dance) and **Nritya** (expressive dance).
 
• Costumes are traditional, made of "Pat" silk, and adorned with Assamese jewelry.

questions.question: How did India's trade policy reforms post-1991 impact the import of capital goods ?

options.text: Linked capital imports only to foreign companies

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduced tariffs and removed licensing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's 1991 trade policy reforms included significant liberalization measures such as **reducing tariffs** on imports to encourage greater economic integration with the global market.
 
• The **abolition of import licensing** requirements for several categories of goods, including capital goods, made it easier for businesses to procure advanced machinery and technology.
 
• These reforms aimed to improve the **competitiveness and efficiency** of domestic industries by enabling access to high-quality imported capital goods.
 
• Prior to 1991, India's trade policy was characterized by high import tariffs and restrictive licensing, which limited the availability of modern machinery for industries.
 
• The reforms were part of a broader strategy to shift from an import-substitution model to an **export-oriented growth model**, promoting industrialization and economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Goods:** These are physical assets like machinery, tools, and equipment used by industries to produce goods and services. They are essential for industrial development and economic growth.
 
• **Tariff Reduction:** A key aspect of trade liberalization, it involves lowering taxes on imported goods to make them more affordable and accessible, fostering competition and innovation.
 
• **Import Licensing:** A regulatory measure that required businesses to obtain government approval to import certain goods. Its removal streamlined trade processes and reduced bureaucratic delays.
 
• **Balance of Payments Crisis (1991):** The economic crisis that triggered India's liberalization reforms, marked by a severe shortage of foreign exchange reserves and high fiscal deficits.
 
• **New Economic Policy (1991):** The policy framework introduced by the Indian government, focusing on liberalization, privatization, and globalization to revive the economy and promote long-term growth.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to be the president of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annie Besant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Annie Besant was the first woman to become the President of the Indian National Congress in 1917.
 
• She was a British social reformer, theosophist, and supporter of Indian self-rule.
 
• Her presidency marked a significant milestone in the Indian freedom struggle, emphasizing the role of women in leadership.
 
• As a leader of the Home Rule Movement, she strongly advocated for India's autonomy from British rule.
 
• Annie Besant's contribution to the Indian independence movement earned her immense respect and admiration from Indians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC):**

 
 
• Founded in 1885, it was the first modern nationalist movement in the colonies of the British Empire.
 
• The INC played a pivotal role in India's freedom struggle against British rule.
 
• It was initially a platform for educated Indians to discuss political and social issues under British administration.
 
 
 
• **Home Rule Movement:**
 
 
• Started by Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1916 to demand self-governance for India within the British Empire.
 
• The movement laid the groundwork for future mass movements led by the Congress.
 
 
 
• **Theosophical Society:**
 
 
• An organization Annie Besant was deeply involved with, promoting spiritual and philosophical ideas.
 
• It influenced her belief in India's cultural and spiritual heritage.
 
 
 
• **Women's Role in the Freedom Struggle:**
 
 
• Annie Besant's presidency highlighted the significance of women's participation in leadership roles during the independence movement.
 
• Later leaders like Sarojini Naidu followed her path, becoming prominent figures in the INC.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of measuring happiness in a country?

options.text: Understanding citizens' mental and emotional well-being

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Understanding citizens' mental and emotional well-being**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Measuring happiness helps governments assess the **mental health and emotional state** of their citizens, which is essential for overall societal well-being.
 
• It provides insights into the quality of life, including factors like job satisfaction, social relationships, and life purpose.
 
• Happiness metrics can guide policymakers to design **better social programs** focused on improving community health and psychological support systems.
 
• Countries like Bhutan use Gross National Happiness (GNH) instead of GDP as a measure of progress, emphasizing the importance of emotional and mental well-being.
 
• This approach fosters a holistic understanding of societal development beyond economic statistics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Happiness (GNH):**

 
 
• GNH is a development philosophy introduced by Bhutan that prioritizes collective happiness and well-being over economic measures like GDP.
 
• It includes domains such as psychological well-being, health, education, cultural diversity, and ecological resilience.
 
 
 
• **Subjective Well-Being (SWB):**
 
 
• SWB refers to how individuals experience and evaluate their lives, including emotional responses and life satisfaction.
 
• It is widely used in studies measuring happiness and quality of life.
 
 
 
• **World Happiness Report:**
 
 
• An annual publication by the United Nations ranking countries based on happiness levels using criteria such as GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, and freedom to make life choices.
 
• It helps in comparing global happiness trends and identifying areas for improvement.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Mental Health:**
 
 
• Good mental health is directly linked to higher levels of happiness and productivity.
 
• Governments often allocate resources to improve mental health services to enhance societal happiness.
 
 
 
• **Happiness Index:**
 
 
• Happiness indices are tools used to measure the general well-being and contentment of populations.
 
• They factor in social, psychological, and economic elements to provide a multidimensional perspective on development.

questions.question: In which year did Toni Morrison become the first African-American woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1993**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Toni Morrison became the first African-American woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in **1993**.
 
• The Nobel Prize was awarded to her for her profound contributions to literature, including works like **"Beloved," "Song of Solomon,"** and **"The Bluest Eye."**
 
• Morrison's writing is celebrated for its rich language and deep exploration of African-American identity, history, and culture.
 
• The Nobel Committee praised her for her **"visionary force and poetic import"** in depicting the lives of African-Americans.
 
• She was the **eighth woman** and the first African-American to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nobel Prize in Literature:** It is one of the five original Nobel Prizes established by Alfred Nobel's will in 1895, awarded annually to authors with outstanding contributions to the field of literature.
 
• **Beloved:** One of Morrison's most acclaimed novels, "Beloved" won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1988 and is considered a masterpiece exploring themes of slavery, motherhood, and identity.
 
• **Other Works:** Toni Morrison’s other notable works include "The Bluest Eye," "Sula," "Tar Baby," and "Jazz," which delve into themes of race, gender, and societal norms.
 
• **Legacy:** Beyond her literary achievements, Morrison was a professor at Princeton University and played a significant role in advancing African-American literature in academic and public spheres.
 
• **Impact:** Morrison’s Nobel win marked a milestone in recognizing African-American voices in global literature and inspired many writers from marginalized communities worldwide.

questions.question: According to Section 21 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha sanhita, 2023, which of the following statements is correct regarding the | trial of offences under Sections 64 to 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?

options.text: The trial must be conducted by any police officer of the rank of DSP and above.
These offences must be tried only in a High Court under a male judge.

__
 
• Section 21 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 emphasizes gender inclusivity in judicial proceedings.
 
• Offences under Sections 64 to 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 are recommended to be tried by courts presided over by women to ensure sensitivity in handling specific cases.
 
• The provision aims to promote a gender-balanced judiciary and foster trust among vulnerable communities.
 
• Although not mandatory, this guideline is designed to ensure fairness and representation in the trial process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023:** This code consolidates laws related to criminal procedures, emphasizing efficiency and justice.
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:** A comprehensive legal framework replacing the Indian Penal Code, focusing on modernization and inclusivity.
 
• **Gender Inclusivity in Judiciary:** Promoting female judges ensures sensitivity in handling gender-based crimes and fosters balanced representation.
 
• **Executive Magistrates:** Officials with administrative authority who occasionally oversee specific legal matters, distinct from judicial magistrates.
 
• **Judicial Reforms in India:** The introduction of updated legal codes like Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita reflects a shift toward modernizing India's judicial system.

questions.question: Bihu is a folk music and dance form associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bihu** is the most celebrated folk music and dance form of **Assam**, symbolizing the cultural identity of the Assamese people.
 
• It is performed during the **Rongali Bihu** festival, which marks the Assamese New Year and the arrival of spring.
 
• The dance is characterized by brisk steps, rapid hand movements, and vibrant costumes.
 
• Musical instruments such as the **dhol** (drum), **pepa** (buffalo horn pipe), and **gagana** (a reed instrument) are commonly used in Bihu performances.
 
• Bihu is not just a dance but a celebration of Assam’s agrarian roots, as it is closely linked to the harvest season.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Bihu:** There are three major types of Bihu celebrated in Assam – Rongali (Bohag) Bihu, Kongali (Kati) Bihu, and Bhogali (Magh) Bihu, each corresponding to different agricultural cycles.
 
• **Rongali Bihu:** This is the most popular form of Bihu, celebrated in April, marking the Assamese New Year and the sowing season.
 
• **Traditional Attire:** During Bihu performances, women wear traditional Assamese attire called **Mekhela Chador**, while men wear **Dhoti and Gamosa**.
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:** Bihu dance has gained international recognition and is often performed at global cultural festivals to represent India’s rich heritage.
 
• **Folk Significance:** Beyond entertainment, Bihu dance serves as a platform to express joy, unity, and gratitude towards nature and the harvest.

questions.question: What is used to measure the health dimension in HDI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Life expectancy at birth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Life expectancy at birth is the primary indicator used to measure the health dimension in the Human Development Index (HDI).
 
• It reflects the average number of years a newborn is expected to live if current mortality rates continue.
 
• This indicator is crucial for understanding the overall health and quality of life in a country or region.
 
• The data for life expectancy is typically sourced from institutions like the United Nations or the World Health Organization (WHO).
 
• It is a composite measure that incorporates the impact of healthcare systems, nutrition, and living conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• HDI is a composite index used to rank countries based on human development levels.
 
• It includes three dimensions: health (measured by life expectancy), education, and standard of living.
 
 
 
• **Other Dimensions of HDI:**
 
 
• Education is measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling.
 
• Standard of living is measured using Gross National Income (GNI) per capita.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Life expectancy indicates the effectiveness of healthcare, sanitation, and social policies in a country.
 
• It serves as a predictor for the quality of life and overall development of a population.
 
 
 
• **Global Patterns:**
 
 
• Countries with higher HDI scores tend to have higher life expectancy due to better healthcare and living standards.
 
• Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia historically report lower life expectancy due to poverty, disease, and limited healthcare access.

questions.question: Bihu, the festival of Assam, is celebrated to mark:

options.text: The victory of good over evil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The new harvest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bihu** is the most prominent cultural festival of Assam, celebrated with enthusiasm by all communities.
 
• The festival marks the **harvest season** and is celebrated to express gratitude to nature and honor the hard work of farmers.
 
• There are three main types of Bihu – **Bohag Bihu** (Rongali Bihu), **Magh Bihu** (Bhogali Bihu), and **Kati Bihu** (Kongali Bihu).
 
• **Bohag Bihu**, celebrated in April, marks the Assamese New Year and the beginning of the sowing season.
 
• **Magh Bihu**, celebrated in January, marks the end of the harvesting season and is accompanied by feasting and bonfires.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rongali Bihu:** Celebrated in April, this is the most vibrant and widely celebrated Bihu. It marks the Assamese New Year and the start of the agricultural cycle.
 
• **Bhogali Bihu:** Also known as Magh Bihu, it is celebrated in January after the harvest, signifying a time of abundance and community feasting.
 
• **Kongali Bihu:** Celebrated in October, this marks the end of the sowing season and is a quieter festival with prayers for a good harvest.
 
• The word "Bihu" originates from the Sanskrit word "**Vishuv**", signifying the solar equinox. It is closely tied to the agrarian lifestyle of Assam.
 
• During Bihu, traditional folk dances and songs like the **Bihu dance** and **Bihu geet** are performed to celebrate joy and prosperity.

questions.question:
Read the following statements carefully:

Statement I: A pressure cooker operates by decreasing the pressure inside, which lowers the boiling point of water.

Statement II: Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because the higher pressure allows water to boil at a temperature above 100°C.

Statement III: The superheated steam within the cooker increases the rate of heat transfer to the food, leading to faster cooking.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.text: Only II and III are correct
All I, II, and III are correct
Only I and II are correct
Only I and III are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1 (Only II and III are correct)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement II:** Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because the higher pressure increases the boiling point of water above 100°C, enabling faster heat transfer to the food.
 
• **Statement III:** Superheated steam generated within the pressure cooker accelerates cooking due to enhanced heat transfer efficiency.
 
• **Statement I:** Incorrect, as a pressure cooker operates by increasing pressure inside, not decreasing it, which raises the boiling point of water.
 
• Pressure cooking is widely used to save time and energy while preparing food due to its efficient heat utilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boiling Point Elevation:** At higher pressure, water boils at temperatures above 100°C, allowing food to cook faster.
 
• **Superheated Steam:** Steam produced at elevated pressure carries more heat energy, leading to efficient cooking processes.
 
• **Working Principle:** Pressure cookers use sealed lids to trap steam, increasing internal pressure and temperature for faster cooking.
 
• **Thermodynamics:** The higher pressure and temperature improve thermal conductivity and heat absorption by the food inside.
 
• Pressure cooking reduces cooking times significantly compared to conventional methods, making it energy-efficient.

questions.question: What is the name of the satellite launched by ISRO's GSLV-F09 that was a gift to SAARC nations ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GSAT-9**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• GSAT-9, also known as the **South Asia Satellite**, was launched by ISRO on **May 5, 2017** using the GSLV-F09 rocket.
 
• The satellite is a **communication satellite** specifically designed as a gift to the SAARC nations, excluding Pakistan.
 
• It provides various services like **telecommunication, television broadcasting, and disaster management support** to participating countries.
 
• GSAT-9 weighs around **2,230 kg** and was developed at an estimated cost of Rs. 235 crore.
 
• The participating countries include India, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation):**

 
 
• SAARC was established in **1985** and includes eight member nations: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.
 
• The organization aims to promote economic and regional integration among South Asian countries.
 
 
 
• **GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle):**
 
 
• It is a launch vehicle developed by ISRO to deploy satellites into geostationary orbits.
 
• GSLV-F09 marks the ninth flight of the GSLV series and uses an indigenously developed cryogenic upper stage.
 
 
 
• **Communication Satellites:**
 
 
• Communication satellites enable the transmission of data, voice, and video across vast distances.
 
• They play a crucial role in applications such as television broadcasting, internet services, and disaster management.
 
 
 
• **Regional Collaboration via GSAT-9:**
 
 
• The satellite fosters regional cooperation by enabling shared technological benefits among SAARC countries.
 
• It helps strengthen India's diplomatic ties with its neighbors through technological assistance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT TRUE about Tribhuvandas Patel?

options.text: He was the founder of the Kaira Milk Union (Amul).

questions.question: How did the administrative roles of rajas differ from those of zamindars under the Mughal system

options.text: Zamindars were subordinate tax officers under the rajas, appointed directly by the emperor.
Rajas and zamindars performed identical roles but differed in their religious affiliations.
Rajas governed broader regions and held a higher status, while zamindars primarily managed land revenue collection.
Zamindars exercised complete political control, whereas rajas held only ceremonial titles.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajas governed broader regions and held a higher status, while zamindars primarily managed land revenue collection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The administrative roles of rajas and zamindars were distinct under the Mughal system, with **rajas holding broader territorial and administrative responsibilities**.
 
• **Zamindars were primarily responsible for collecting land revenue** on behalf of the Mughal emperor and acted as intermediaries between the peasants and the state.
 
• Rajas often governed larger regions and were seen as **local rulers or chieftains** with higher status and power compared to zamindars.
 
• Zamindars did not exercise complete political control but were vital for the revenue system, while rajas had **both administrative and ceremonial roles**.
 
• This hierarchical structure ensured a decentralized but efficient administration under the Mughal empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamindars:**

 
 
• Zamindars were landowners or revenue collectors who were granted the right to collect taxes from peasants.
 
• They retained a portion of the revenue as their income and remitted the rest to the state treasury.
 
• They did not have sovereignty but played a crucial role in the agrarian economy.
 
 
 
• **Rajas:**
 
 
• Rajas were local or regional rulers who often held hereditary titles.
 
• They enjoyed a higher status compared to zamindars and had a broader administrative role, including managing military and governance affairs.
 
• Many rajas retained their autonomy under the Mughal system by acknowledging Mughal supremacy and paying tribute.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Revenue System:**
 
 
• The Mughal administration used a hierarchical system of governance to ensure efficient tax collection and local control.
 
• Zamindars were an integral part of this system, ensuring the flow of revenue from the grassroots to the empire.
 
 
 
• **Decentralized Governance:**
 
 
• The Mughal empire relied on a decentralized system, allowing local rulers like rajas and zamindars to handle regional administration while maintaining allegiance to the emperor.
 
• This model helped manage the vast and diverse territories of the Mughal empire efficiently.

questions.question:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:

Statement 1: Karnataka has the highest elephant population among Southern States.

Statement 2: A high number of juvenile elephant deaths in Karnataka are due to Elephant Endotheliotropic Herpesvirus (EEHV).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Statements 1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Karnataka has the highest elephant population** among Southern states, as per the latest elephant census conducted by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
 
• According to reports, Karnataka is home to over **6,000 elephants**, the largest population in Southern India.
 
• Juvenile elephant deaths in Karnataka have been linked to **Elephant Endotheliotropic Herpesvirus (EEHV)**, a fatal viral disease affecting young elephants.
 
• EEHV primarily impacts elephants aged between 1 and 8 years, causing severe internal hemorrhaging and often death within days of infection.
 
• Efforts are being made to improve monitoring, diagnosis, and treatment of EEHV, including collaborations between veterinarians, conservationists, and wildlife organizations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asian Elephants:** India is home to the largest population of Asian elephants, and they are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
 
• **Elephant Endotheliotropic Herpesvirus (EEHV):** A highly fatal virus that affects young elephants, with symptoms including lethargy, reduced appetite, and hemorrhagic symptoms.
 
• **Conservation Efforts:** The government has initiated projects like Project Elephant, which aims to ensure the long-term survival of elephants in their natural habitats.
 
• **Elephant Corridors:** Karnataka has several elephant corridors that are crucial for the free movement and migration of elephants, reducing human-elephant conflict.
 
• **Wildlife Health Monitoring:** Advanced veterinary facilities and research are being deployed to tackle diseases like EEHV and improve elephant health care.

questions.question: In the lac operon model, what is the primary role of the allolactose molecule?

options.text: It functions as an inducer, binding to the repressor protein and inactivating it.
It acts as a corepressor, binding with the repressor protein.
It binds to the promoter to initiate transcription.
It directly codes for the enzymes involved in lactose metabolism.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It functions as an inducer, binding to the repressor protein and inactivating it.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Allolactose acts as an **inducer** in the lac operon, which is a genetic regulatory system in bacteria.
 
• It binds to the **repressor protein**, causing a conformational change that inactivates the repressor.
 
• When the repressor is inactivated, it can no longer bind to the operator region, allowing transcription of genes responsible for lactose metabolism.
 
• This process ensures that the enzymes needed for lactose metabolism are produced only when lactose is present in the environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lac operon:** It is a cluster of genes in Escherichia coli that are involved in lactose metabolism. It includes structural genes like lacZ, lacY, and lacA.
 
• **Repressor protein (lacI):** A regulatory protein that binds to the operator region of the lac operon to block transcription when lactose is absent.
 
• **Operator region:** A segment of DNA in the lac operon where the repressor protein binds to prevent transcription.
 
• **Allolactose:** A derivative of lactose formed by the action of β-galactosidase. It serves as the signaling molecule (inducer) for the lac operon.
 
• **Inducible operon:** The lac operon is an example of an inducible operon, which is activated in the presence of an inducer molecule like allolactose.

**(Denudational Processes) **

 
 
 
**Column B **

 Weathering

 kinetic Energy

 Mass Movement

 Gravitational / Molecular stresses / chemical Actions
 
 

 
 
C.

 
 Erosion and Transportation
 
 
3.

 
 Gravitational Force
 
 

 
 
D.

 
 Denudation (overall process)
 
 
4.

 
 External Forces acting on Earth surface
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1 (A - 2, B - 3, C - 1, D - 4)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Weathering** is primarily driven by gravitational, molecular stresses, and chemical actions__, which operate at a micro-level to disintegrate rocks (A - 2).
 
• **Mass Movement** is caused by the __gravitational force__ acting on weathered materials, leading to downhill movement (B - 3).
 
• **Erosion and Transportation** involve the action of __kinetic energy__, typically from water, wind, or ice, to remove and relocate surface materials (C - 1).
 
• **Denudation** is the overall process driven by __external forces__, including weathering, erosion, and mass movement, acting on Earth's surface (D - 4).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Weathering:**

 
 
• A natural process where rocks disintegrate without any major movement.
 
• Can be mechanical (physical), chemical, or biological in nature.
 
• Examples include frost action, oxidation, and root growth.
 
 
 
• **Mass Movement:**
 
 
• Involves the downward movement of soil, rock, and debris due to gravity.
 
• Examples include landslides, rockfalls, and soil creep.
 
• Factors like water saturation and slope steepness influence the rate of movement.
 
 
 
• **Erosion and Transportation:**
 
 
• Refers to the detachment and movement of surface materials by agents like water, wind, glaciers, and waves.
 
• Transportation distributes the eroded material to different locations.
 
• River systems, coastal waves, and windstorms are common examples.
 
 
 
• **Denudation:**
 
 
• It is the collective term for processes like weathering, mass movement, erosion, and transportation.
 
• Denudation contributes to the reduction of Earth's surface by leveling highlands and filling basins.
 
• It is a key factor in shaping landforms over geological time.

questions.question: Which entities are eligible to register under the FCRA?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Section 8 companies, trusts, and societies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) allows **Section 8 companies, trusts, and societies** to register for receiving foreign contributions.
 
• Section 8 companies are non-profit entities established under the Companies Act, 2013, with the objective of promoting charitable, educational, or social welfare activities.
 
• Trusts and societies are also eligible under FCRA, provided they are registered and fulfill the prescribed norms.
 
• The primary purpose of FCRA registration is to ensure that foreign contributions are used for legal, transparent, and socially beneficial purposes.
 
• Entities like political parties, government departments, and private companies are **not eligible** for FCRA registration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA), 2010:**

 
 
• FCRA regulates the acceptance and utilization of foreign funds by individuals, associations, or companies in India.
 
• The primary objective is to prevent the misuse of foreign contributions and ensure that they are not used for activities detrimental to national interest.
 
 
 
• **Section 8 Companies:**
 
 
• These are non-profit organizations incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013.
 
• Their main goal is to promote commerce, art, science, education, research, social welfare, religion, or environmental protection.
 
 
 
• **Registration under FCRA:**
 
 
• Entities must apply to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) for FCRA registration.
 
• Once registered, these entities are allowed to receive foreign contributions for approved projects.
 
 
 
• **Prohibited Entities:**
 
 
• Political parties, electoral candidates, media organizations, and government employees are prohibited from accepting foreign funds under FCRA.
 
 
 
• **Recent Updates:**
 
 
• The FCRA rules were amended in 2020 to tighten regulations, including restrictions on administrative expenses and mandatory use of an SBI account for foreign fund transactions.

questions.question: What evidence supports the Big Bang theory of universe origin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Redshift of galaxies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The redshift of galaxies indicates that the universe is expanding, which supports the Big Bang theory.
 
• The phenomenon of redshift was first observed by Edwin Hubble, who discovered a direct relationship between a galaxy's distance and its velocity of recession (Hubble's Law).
 
• This redshift occurs due to the Doppler effect, where light waves stretch as objects (galaxies) move away from the observer.
 
• The discovery of the cosmic microwave background radiation also aligns with the redshift observations, further corroborating the theory.
 
• Redshift is measured by observing the displacement of spectral lines toward the red end of the spectrum in light emitted from distant galaxies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Big Bang Theory:** The theory states that the universe originated approximately 13.8 billion years ago from an extremely hot and dense singularity, followed by rapid expansion.
 
• **Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation (CMB):** Discovered in 1965 by Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson, CMB is the faint radiation left over from the Big Bang, providing strong evidence for the theory.
 
• **Hubble's Law:** This law states that the recessional velocity of a galaxy is directly proportional to its distance from the observer, confirming the expanding nature of the universe.
 
• **Doppler Effect:** A change in the frequency or wavelength of light or sound waves caused by the relative movement of the source and the observer. In astronomy, it explains the redshift of galaxies moving away.
 
• **Redshift (z):** A dimensionless measure used in astronomy to quantify the extent to which light from a celestial object has been stretched due to its motion away from the observer.

questions.question: Who was the Chairman of the "Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, and Tribal and Excluded Areas in the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the **Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, and Tribal and Excluded Areas** in the Constituent Assembly.
 
• The Advisory Committee was formed to address the critical issues of **minorities and fundamental rights** during the drafting of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Under his leadership, the committee played a key role in shaping the provisions related to **equality, justice, and protection of minority rights**.
 
• The committee's recommendations significantly influenced the drafting of **Part III (Fundamental Rights) and Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Sardar Patel’s leadership ensured a balanced approach to addressing the concerns of various communities while maintaining national unity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**

 
 
• Known as the **Iron Man of India**, Patel played a pivotal role in the integration of princely states into the Indian Union.
 
• He was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India.
 
• Patel's efforts in unifying the country earned him the title of **Bismarck of India**.
 
 
 
• **Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• This committee was one of the most important committees in the Constituent Assembly.
 
• It was tasked with addressing sensitive issues such as **minority rights, tribal welfare, and excluded areas**.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• These rights are enshrined in **Part III of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• They guarantee civil liberties and ensure equality, justice, and freedom for Indian citizens.
 
• Examples include the **Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, and Right against Exploitation**.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**
 
 
• These principles are included in **Part IV of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• They aim to establish a framework for creating a just society in India.
 
• Although not enforceable by law, they serve as guidelines for the government in policymaking.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements comparing the Simon Commission (1927) and the Nehru Report (1928):

1. The Simon Commission was boycotted by Indian political parties primarily due to its all-Indian composition.

2. The Nehru Report proposed complete independence for India as its immediate objective.

Which of the above is / are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither 1 nor 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1 is incorrect:** The Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted by Indian political parties primarily because it lacked any Indian representation, not because of its "all-Indian composition." The commission consisted solely of British members, leading to widespread protests.
 
• **Statement 2 is incorrect:** The Nehru Report (1928), authored by Motilal Nehru, advocated for "Dominion Status" for India within the British Empire, not complete independence. The demand for complete independence was officially adopted later in 1929 during the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The Simon Commission was tasked with reviewing the Government of India Act, 1919, and recommending constitutional reforms, but it was met with hostility due to its exclusion of Indians from the process.
 
• The Nehru Report marked a significant effort by Indian leaders to draft a constitution for self-governance, but it fell short of the aspirations of younger leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose, who sought complete independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simon Commission (1927):**

 
 
• Officially known as the Indian Statutory Commission, it was led by Sir John Simon and consisted entirely of British members, which was a major point of contention.
 
• Its arrival in India was met with protests and slogans like "Simon Go Back." Leaders like Lala Lajpat Rai played a key role in opposing it.
 
• The commission's recommendations eventually led to the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
 
 
• **Nehru Report (1928):**
 
 
• This was the first attempt by Indians to draft a constitutional framework for India.
 
• It proposed a parliamentary system of governance, protection of minority rights, and fundamental rights but fell short of demanding complete independence.
 
• Its rejection by the British and the failure to meet the aspirations of younger leaders led to a shift in Congress's stance toward the demand for complete independence.
 
 
 
• **Lahore Session (1929):**
 
 
• In this session, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Indian National Congress officially adopted "Purna Swaraj" (Complete Independence) as its goal.
 
• 26th January 1930 was declared as Independence Day, which is now celebrated as Republic Day in remembrance of this declaration.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935:**
 
 
• This act was influenced by the Simon Commission's recommendations and introduced provincial autonomy and the federal structure in India.
 
• It served as a precursor to India's constitutional development leading up to independence.

questions.question: Name the state in which The Bhitarkanika Mangroves are located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bhitarkanika Mangroves** are located in Kendrapara district of Odisha, India.
 
• It is the **second-largest mangrove ecosystem** in India after the Sundarbans in West Bengal.
 
• The area is home to the **Bhitarkanika National Park**, a biodiversity hotspot known for its rich flora and fauna.
 
• Bhitarkanika Mangroves are famous for hosting **saltwater crocodiles**, including one of the largest crocodiles ever recorded.
 
• This region is protected under the **Ramsar Convention** as a wetland of international importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mangroves**: These are coastal vegetation found in tropical and subtropical regions, characterized by their ability to thrive in saline and brackish waters.
 
• **Ramsar Convention**: An international treaty signed in 1971 for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands.
 
• **Bhitarkanika National Park**: It spans over 672 square kilometers and is known for its estuarine ecosystem, mudflats, and tidal rivers.
 
• The region is also recognized for its **diverse avian population**, including migratory birds from Europe and Central Asia.
 
• Bhitarkanika is home to rare species like the **Indian Python, King Cobra, and Olive Ridley Turtles**, which nest on nearby beaches.

options.text: Mission Shakti - Startup grants for rural men

__

questions.question: The Vesara style of temple architecture is a combination of which two styles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravidian and Nagara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vesara style of temple architecture is a **fusion of Dravidian and Nagara styles**, prominently seen in the Deccan region of India.
 
• This style emerged during the rule of the **Chalukyas of Badami** (6th-8th centuries CE) and further evolved under the Hoysalas (12th-13th centuries CE).
 
• **Dravidian style** originated in South India, known for its pyramidal towers (vimanas) and intricately carved structures.
 
• **Nagara style** is a North Indian architectural tradition, characterized by beehive-shaped towers (shikharas) and the absence of elaborate boundary walls.
 
• The Vesara style incorporates a mix of both elements, with **curvilinear towers** and intricate carvings, making it distinct and versatile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:**

 
 
• **Vimana:** The pyramidal tower above the sanctum in Dravidian temples.
 
• **Shikhara:** The curvilinear or pyramidal tower in Nagara temples.
 
• **Garbha Griha:** The sanctum sanctorum where the deity resides in temples.
 
 
 
• The Chalukyas of Badami were instrumental in blending the Nagara and Dravidian styles, resulting in the Vesara style. Examples include the temples at Pattadakal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• Examples of Vesara temples include the **Virupaksha Temple** at Pattadakal and the **Chennakesava Temple** at Belur (Hoysala era).
 
• The Hoysalas further refined the Vesara style, introducing **soapstone carvings** and star-shaped platforms in their temples.
 
• The Vesara style is often referred to as the **"middle style"** due to its geographical and stylistic position between the Dravidian South and Nagara North.

questions.question: Whom Hiuen Tsang called "one of the four lights of world", who's also called Indian Einstein ?

• His philosophical concepts, particularly the doctrine of "Shunyata" (emptiness), are considered revolutionary in Buddhist thought.
 
• Due to his profound intellect and transformative contributions to philosophy and metaphysics, Nagarjuna is often referred to as the "Indian Einstein."
 
• He lived during the 2nd–3rd century CE and his works significantly influenced Buddhist traditions and Indian intellectual history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Madhyamaka Philosophy:** Nagarjuna's school of thought emphasized the "Middle Way," avoiding extremes of eternalism and nihilism.
 
• **Scientific Analogies:** Nagarjuna's philosophical inquiries into causality and interdependence are compared to modern scientific principles, earning him the title "Indian Einstein."
 
• **Contributions to Medicine and Alchemy:** Nagarjuna is also credited with advancements in Ayurveda and early Indian alchemical traditions.
 
• **Works:** His major treatises include "Mula-Madhyamaka-Karika" (Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way) and other texts exploring Buddhist metaphysics.

• The time limit aims to ensure speedy justice to the victims of child abuse and prevent prolonged trauma.
 
• This provision is mandated under **Section 35** of the POCSO Act, 2012, which emphasizes the importance of expediting child-related cases.
 
• The Act requires that all proceedings, including evidence collection and judgment, are conducted in a **child-friendly manner** to minimize distress for the victim.
 
• The one-year time frame is part of broader measures introduced to strengthen the judicial framework for protecting children’s rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The POCSO Act was enacted to address the issue of sexual exploitation and abuse of children and provides safeguards for children at every stage of the judicial process.

• These courts are equipped with trained professionals to handle child witnesses and evidence collection.
 
 
 
• **Child-friendly Procedures:**
 
 
• POCSO emphasizes that the statement of the child victim should be recorded at their residence or a place of their choice in the presence of a trusted adult.
 
• Cross-examinations are conducted in-camera to prevent further trauma to the child.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Obligations:**
 
 
• The Act makes it mandatory for any person with knowledge of a child being sexually abused to report the incident to the police.

questions.question: Which discretionary power allows a Governor to reserve a bill passed by the state legislature for the consideration of the President?

options.text: To send a report to the President for the imposition of President's Rule.
To reserve a bill for the President's consideration.
To grant pardon in certain cases.
To summon, prorogue, and dissolve the state legislative assembly.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To reserve a bill for the President's consideration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor has a discretionary power under Article **200** of the Indian Constitution to reserve certain types of bills passed by the State Legislature for the **consideration of the President**.
 
• This power is exercised when the bill in question may violate the Constitution or conflict with the **Union Laws**.
 
• Once reserved, the President can either give assent, withhold assent, or return the bill for **reconsideration** (except for money bills).
 
• Such bills can only become a law if the President grants their assent, making it a critical aspect of the balance between the **State and Union** governments.
 
• The Governor does not need the advice of the Council of Ministers when deciding to reserve a bill for the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 200 of the Indian Constitution:** This article empowers the Governor to take specific actions on bills passed by the State Legislature, including withholding assent, reserving the bill for the President, or returning it (except money bills).
 
• **Scope of Discretionary Power:** The Governor exercises this power independently, without consulting the State Council of Ministers.
 
• **President's Role:** Once a bill is reserved, the President can assent, withhold assent, or return the bill (if not a money bill) for reconsideration by the State Legislature.
 
• **Significance:** This mechanism ensures that state legislation adheres to the provisions of the Constitution and does not encroach upon Union powers.
 
• **Limitation:** The Governor cannot reserve every bill; the bill must meet certain conditions, such as potential conflict with the Constitution or Union interests.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is incorrect regarding global indices as of July 2025?

options.text: The World Happiness Report 2024 highlights social support, life expectancy, and GDP per capita as key happiness factors.
AQI consistently above 200 signals general health risks and requires urgent policy action.
Despite being discontinued, the Ease of Doing Business report remains influential for investors assessing startup procedures.
A rise in GNI per capita alone can significantly improve HDI, even with falling life expectancy and education.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) is calculated using three primary indicators: life expectancy, education (mean years and expected years), and GNI per capita (Gross National Income).
 
• A rise in GNI per capita alone cannot significantly improve the HDI score if other parameters like life expectancy and education decline.
 
• The HDI approach emphasizes balanced improvement across all dimensions for holistic human development assessment.
 
• Global HDI rankings and trends reflect a country's socio-economic and public health development over time.
 
• The claim that "a rise in GNI per capita alone can significantly improve HDI, even with falling life expectancy and education" is incorrect, as HDI depends on simultaneous performance across all indicators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• Developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to measure a country's overall achievement in its social and economic dimensions.
 
• HDI is a composite index based on three dimensions: health (life expectancy), education, and standard of living (GNI per capita).
 
• It is widely used to compare development levels among nations and regions.
 
 
 
• **Gross National Income (GNI):**
 
 
• GNI represents the total income earned by a country's residents and businesses, including income from abroad.
 
• It is an important economic indicator used in HDI calculation to reflect the standard of living.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Life expectancy serves as a proxy for the health dimension in HDI.
 
• It reflects the average number of years a person is expected to live, based on current mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **Education Indicators in HDI:**
 
 
• Mean years of schooling (average years of education received by people aged 25 and older).
 
• Expected years of schooling (number of years a child of school-entry age is expected to spend in school).
 
 
 
• **Balanced Development:**
 
 
• Improvement in one dimension (e.g., GNI) cannot compensate for declines in others (e.g., education or health).
 
• Holistic growth across all dimensions is crucial for sustainable human development.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the life cycle of a star like the Sun?

options.text: Protostar - White Dwarf - Red Giant - Main Sequence
Nebula - Red Giant - Main Sequence - White Dwarf
Main Sequence - Red Giant - White Dwarf

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Main Sequence - Red Giant - White Dwarf**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A star like the Sun begins its life in the **Main Sequence stage**, where it fuses hydrogen into helium in its core, releasing energy.
 
• Once the hydrogen in the core is exhausted, the star expands into a **Red Giant**, where helium fusion occurs in the core, and hydrogen fusion continues in a shell around the core.
 
• After the Red Giant phase, the outer layers of the star are ejected, forming a planetary nebula, leaving behind the core as a **White Dwarf**.
 
• A **White Dwarf** is a dense, dim, and cooling remnant composed mostly of carbon and oxygen.
 
• The Sun-like star's life cycle ends with the White Dwarf gradually cooling over billions of years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nebula:** A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in space, which can collapse under gravity to form a protostar, the initial stage of a star's life.
 
• **Main Sequence:** This is the longest and most stable phase in a star's life cycle, where it spends most of its life fusing hydrogen into helium.
 
• **Red Giant:** A stage where the star expands significantly and becomes cooler and brighter as it starts fusing helium.
 
• **White Dwarf:** The final stage of a Sun-like star, where nuclear fusion has ceased, and the star is supported by electron degeneracy pressure.
 
• **Planetary Nebula:** A colorful shell of ionized gas ejected from a Red Giant at the end of its life, surrounding the newly formed White Dwarf.

questions.question: A conductor of length L and resistance R is cut into two equal halves. These two halves are then connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance of this parallel combination?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**R/4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a conductor of length L and resistance R is cut into two equal halves, the resistance of each half becomes **R/2**.
 
• If these two halves are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination is given by the formula for parallel resistors: **1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2**.
 
• Substituting R1 = R/2 and R2 = R/2, the calculation becomes **1/Req = 2/(R/2) = 4/R**.
 
• Therefore, the equivalent resistance of the combination is **Req = R/4**.
 
• This result arises due to the inverse relationship of resistance in parallel circuits, which reduces the overall resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistance in Parallel Combination:**

 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the reciprocal of the total resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of individual resistances: **1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...**.
 
• Parallel connections lead to a decrease in the overall resistance due to the multiple paths for current flow.
 
 
 
• **Resistance and Length Relationship:**
 
 
• The resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to its length (R ∝ L).
 
• When the conductor is divided into two equal parts, the resistance of each part becomes half of the original.
 
 
 
• **Ohm’s Law:**
 
 
• Ohm’s Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points and inversely proportional to the resistance.
 
• The formula is **V = IR**, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
 
 
• **Applications:** Understanding parallel and series resistance is crucial in designing electrical circuits for household appliances, power distribution, and electronic systems.
 
• **Practical Observation:** In real-world scenarios, parallel circuits are preferred in many cases as they ensure that a failure in one path does not disrupt the entire circuit.

questions.question: During the period of 1947-1990, India's trade policy was largely characterized by:

options.text: An inward-looking strategy emphasizing import substitution and protection of domestic industries.
A policy of free trade with minimal government intervention in international transactions.
A liberal import policy aimed at providing consumers with a wide range of goods.
An aggressive export-oriented strategy focused on global competitiveness.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An inward-looking strategy emphasizing import substitution and protection of domestic industries.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's trade policy between 1947-1990 was focused on **self-reliance**, aiming to reduce dependence on foreign goods and foster domestic industries.
 
• The strategy of **import substitution industrialization (ISI)** was adopted to protect and promote local industries by imposing high tariffs and quantitative restrictions on imports.
 
• This policy was driven by the belief that economic independence was essential for political independence and to avoid exploitation by foreign powers.
 
• India emphasized the development of heavy industries and basic infrastructure through public sector enterprises, which were seen as a means to achieve self-sufficiency.
 
• The trade policy was restrictive, with controls on foreign exchange and limited engagement in global trade, aiming to insulate the domestic economy from external influences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Import Substitution Industrialization (ISI):**

 
 
• This strategy focuses on replacing imported goods with domestically produced goods to strengthen local industries.
 
• It was widely adopted by newly independent countries, including India, during the mid-20th century.
 
• While it initially boosted industrial growth, ISI often led to inefficiencies and a lack of competitiveness in global markets.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of India's Pre-1991 Trade Policy:**
 
 
• High tariffs and import licensing to discourage imports.
 
• Focus on heavy industries, public sector dominance, and central planning under the Five-Year Plans.
 
• Limited foreign direct investment (FDI) and restricted access to foreign technology.
 
 
 
• **Protectionism:**
 
 
• Protective measures such as tariffs, quotas, and subsidies were used to shield domestic industries from international competition.
 
• This approach aimed to nurture infant industries but often resulted in inefficiencies and lack of innovation.
 
 
 
• **Shift Post-1991:**
 
 
• India shifted to a liberalized trade regime in 1991, focusing on globalization, privatization, and economic reforms.
 
• The introduction of reforms marked a departure from protectionism to outward-oriented policies, integrating India into the global economy.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of meristematic tissues in plants?

options.text: Large vacuoles and thick cell walls
Absence of nucleus and presence of lignified walls
Actively dividing cells with dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei
Dead cells that provide mechanical support

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Actively dividing cells with dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Meristematic tissues** consist of actively dividing cells that are responsible for plant growth.
 
• Cells in meristematic tissues have a **dense cytoplasm** and lack large vacuoles, which allows efficient division.
 
• These cells possess **prominent nuclei** to control cell division and metabolic activities.
 
• The cell walls in meristematic tissues are **thin and non-lignified**, facilitating flexibility during cell division.
 
• Meristematic tissues are located in specific regions such as **apical meristems, lateral meristems, and intercalary meristems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apical Meristems**: Found at the tips of roots and shoots, responsible for primary growth (increase in length).
 
• **Lateral Meristems**: Located in the sides of stems and roots, responsible for secondary growth (increase in thickness).
 
• **Intercalary Meristems**: Present at the base of leaves or internodes, aiding in regrowth of grass and other monocots.
 
• Meristematic cells lack **large vacuoles** because vacuoles are primarily used for storage, which is not needed during active division.
 
• Meristematic cells eventually differentiate into permanent tissues, which perform specific functions such as support, transport, or photosynthesis.

questions.question: What does the "invisible hand' concept, as proposed by Adam Smith, primarily signify?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Market equilibrium achieved via self-interest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "invisible hand" is a metaphor introduced by Adam Smith in his seminal work "The Wealth of Nations" (1776).
 
• It signifies how individual self-interest in a free-market economy leads to the efficient allocation of resources, benefiting society as a whole.
 
• The concept emphasizes that when individuals pursue their own economic interests, they unintentionally contribute to the overall economic welfare.
 
• Market equilibrium is achieved without explicit intervention due to the natural adjustment of supply and demand forces.
 
• This self-regulating mechanism is a cornerstone of classical economics, advocating minimal government interference in markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adam Smith**: Known as the "Father of Economics," Adam Smith introduced foundational concepts in economics, including the division of labor and free-market principles.
 
• **Free Market Economy**: An economic system where prices and production are determined by unrestricted competition between privately owned businesses.
 
• **Self-Interest**: In economics, self-interest refers to individuals focusing on their personal gain, which indirectly drives innovation, productivity, and societal benefits.
 
• **Market Equilibrium**: The state in which market supply equals demand, resulting in stable prices and optimal resource allocation.
 
• **Criticism of the Invisible Hand**: Critics argue that unchecked markets can lead to inequality, monopolies, and negative externalities, necessitating some level of government intervention.

questions.question: Which of the following High Courts has jurisdiction over more than one state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guwahati High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Guwahati High Court** has jurisdiction over multiple states, including Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• It was originally established as the **High Court of Assam** in 1948 and later renamed as the Guwahati High Court in 1971.
 
• The court operates through its principal seat in Guwahati and has permanent benches in Nagaland, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• This multi-state jurisdiction is unique and ensures legal administration across the northeastern region of India.
 
• The Guwahati High Court plays a crucial role in addressing legal matters pertinent to the northeastern states, which have distinct cultural and legal frameworks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jurisdiction**: Jurisdiction refers to the official power of a court to make legal decisions and judgments. In India, High Courts generally have jurisdiction over one state or union territory.
 
• **Permanent Benches**: Permanent benches are established in cities other than the principal seat of the High Court to cater to specific regions for better access to justice.
 
• **High Courts in India**: India has 25 High Courts, each serving one or more states/union territories. They are the principal civil courts and have appellate jurisdiction over lower courts.
 
• **Assam Accord**: The Guwahati High Court has played a pivotal role in interpreting legal aspects of the Assam Accord, signed in 1985, which addresses issues related to illegal immigration and citizenship in Assam.
 
• **Legal Framework in Northeast India**: The northeastern states have unique legal frameworks, including customary laws and special provisions under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, which are often adjudicated by the Guwahati High Court.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the population growth phase in India with its key characteristic?

options.text: Phase IV (Post-1981) sudden increase in fertility rate due to migration
Phase III (1951-1981) Population explosion caused by falling death rate and high fertility
Phase I (1901-1921) - Rapid population explosion due to low mortality and high fertility
Phase II (1921-1951) High mortality rate and declining birth rate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phase III (1951-1981) Population explosion caused by falling death rate and high fertility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Phase III (1951-1981) marked a significant population explosion in India due to a sharp decline in the death rate while fertility rates remained high.
 
• Improved healthcare services, advancements in medical technology, and public health measures reduced mortality rates significantly during this period.
 
• Developmental policies and food security measures like the Green Revolution ensured better nutrition and survival rates.
 
• This phase saw rapid urbanization and migration to cities, contributing to population growth in urban areas.
 
• The increase in population during Phase III laid the groundwork for economic changes and challenges in resource distribution, education, and employment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phase I (1901-1921):** Characterized by stagnant population growth due to high mortality rates caused by epidemics, famines, and poor living conditions.
 
• **Phase II (1921-1951):** Showed a gradual decline in mortality rates, but birth rates remained high, leading to slow population growth.
 
• **Phase IV (Post-1981):** Marked by declining fertility rates due to increased awareness, family planning measures, and improved socio-economic conditions.
 
• **Demographic Transition Theory:** Explains how population growth transitions from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates as a country develops economically and socially.
 
• **Population Explosion:** Refers to a rapid increase in population due to a combination of falling death rates and sustained high birth rates, often associated with improved healthcare and living conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is an erosional landform created primarily by river action?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gorge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, primarily formed by the erosional action of a river cutting through hard rocks over geological timescales.
 
• It is characterized by vertical walls and is often associated with high-energy rivers that erode the bedrock quickly.
 
• Gorges are commonly found in mountainous regions where rivers flow with high velocity, carving out narrow channels.
 
• Famous examples include the Grand Canyon in the USA, formed by the Colorado River, and Kali Gandaki Gorge in Nepal.
 
• Gorges differ from canyons in their narrower dimensions and steeper walls, making them distinct erosional landforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moraine:** Moraines are depositional landforms created by glaciers, consisting of accumulated debris (rocks and sediments) left behind after glacial movement.
 
• **Delta:** A delta is a depositional landform formed at the mouth of a river where it meets a standing water body like a sea or lake, causing sediment deposition.
 
• **Levee:** Levees are natural or artificial embankments along riverbanks, formed by sediment deposition during flood events.
 
• **River Erosion:** River erosion involves processes like hydraulic action, abrasion, and solution, where water flows remove material from the riverbed and banks.
 
• **Fluvial Landforms:** Erosional landforms like gorges and valleys, and depositional landforms like floodplains and deltas, are collectively termed fluvial landforms.
